| [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) v3 | Sortings conflict as arrangements, not facts | What is directionally right in the owner's LEGO monograph, as Mathematics of Meaning graded it. Its contextuality claim is empty: any sortings of bricks share a joint refinement ([MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md)), and the events they generate stay Boolean ([MOM-ARG-047](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/arguments.d/ARG-047.md)). Its intuition that builders cannot share a sorting is true of arrangements. One set of bins realizes one partition, the product may need more bins than there are, and the cheapest choice depends on what each builder searches for and on what stands out within a bin ([CASE-095](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-095.md)). The disagreement is a trade, not a failure of global truth. Sorting on one attribute also turns a search for a combination of features into a search for one feature within each bin, which Treisman and Gelade (LIT-1082, read) show is the difference between a serial scan and one found at a glance. | Active |

| [CLAIM-313](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-313.md) v2 | With copies, overlapping partitions coexist | Filed at the owner's request, from the readings on locality-sensitive hashing (Indyk and Motwani 1998; Andoni, Laarhoven, Razenshteyn and Waingarten 2017) set against [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md)'s premise that "a set of k bins realizes one partition of the collection at a time".
